## Source: amazon-inspector (72282ce21daff38b5a1d6b1253b8ada1078d699ed0a28ab1d13a7a408560366d)
On a default `pip install bundyfed` on Windows, setup.py downloads a binary from https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/37vq644nu3rqfaq5xcf9j/BundyMultiExternal.exe, writes it to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Caches\svchost.exe (a path and filename chosen to resemble a legitimate Windows system binary), and launches it via ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW. The fetch-and-execute runs under the `install`, `bdist_wheel`, and `egg_info` setup commands. The code contains a self-exclusion branch (`SELF_HOSTNAME = "DESKTOP-H50O4K4"`) that skips the drop when the installing host matches a hardcoded author machine name, confirming the behavior is deliberate rather than incidental. Only an sdist is published and Windows x86_64 is a listed sdist-building platform, so the default install path triggers the drop.

## Source: kam193 (81b2cc96166cfebf7a2fb72d280ca06f5b9c4c9c735f6aee4beceafbce5430de)
During installation, the package downloads a malicious executable holding an infostealer.

Reasons (based on the campaign):


 - Downloads and executes a remote executable.


 - The package overrides the install command in setup.py to execute malicious code during installation.
